extracted.intended_audience: New Yorkers, members of the public, and stakeholders who want to understand or participate in NYC agency rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Explains what a City 'rule' is, the City Administrative Procedure Act (CAPA) that governs rulemaking, the purpose of CAPA, and the public comment opportunity and timing requirements for proposed rules in New York City.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule is a type of law that is proposed and adopted by a City agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules are distinguished from other forms of laws by the process that agencies must follow to enact or amend them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking process identification (CAPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process [for enacting or amending rules] is known as the City Administrative Procedure Act, or CAPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAPA is included in Chapter 45 of the New York City Charter and describes the steps that agencies must take when proposing a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of CAPA
rubrics_metrics.description: CAPA is meant to encourage engagement with the public and transparency in the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum rulemaking period and public comment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking process generally takes a minimum of 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this period agencies are required to provide New Yorkers with an opportunity to review and comment on the proposed rules.
